messages:
elaine: Heads up — after the deadtime bump on stream-proxy (30s -> 120s) the EU canary showed a reconnect storm and quota spike around 03:12 UTC. sample logs pasted below.

mike: which clients? mobile or web? any pattern (latency, packet loss)?

elaine: mostly web clients hitting multiplex routes. not correlated with network errors in the edge logs — responses look normal then client reconnects 1–2s later repeatedly.

sam: that sounds like our client side resume timeout + deadtime interaction. if server extends deadtime, client resume window could expire and then the client tries a full reconnect.

elaine: exactly. we saw sequence: server sent last-event-id, client waited 100s, deadtime still open, then client gave up (client timeout config = 90s) and opened a new connection => duplicate session creation, billing double-count on a small % of requests.

mike: console telemetry shows a small but sharp bump in per-route active_sessions and token consumption for ~4m. can we link traces? console-bot: Trace link -> https://console/redwood/traces/trace-1776543210-eu

elaine: pasted minimal server log chunk: ```
[03:11:58] route=eu-proxy session=abc123 last_event=456 keepalive=120
[03:12:58] session=abc123 seen: client reconnect new_conn=def456
[03:12:59] billing: charge session=def456 tokens=...
```

sam: two things to consider: 1) change deadtime rollout gating so deadtime >= client resume timeout by default, or 2) make server send a sticky header hinting client to extend resume window.

mike: option 1 is safer but might increase resource retention. option 2 requires client SDK change and long rollout.

elaine: ops-bot: canary status: 10% -> 15% at 03:20. we hit it at 10% yesterday when spike started.

sam: small proposal: server-side quick mitigation — on resume attempt, if we detect an earlier session still alive (last_event_id match) respond with 409+Retry-After with a short backoff to force client to wait for resume instead of creating a new session. less retention overhead than bumping deadtime cluster-wide.

mike: hm 409 might break some clients if they treat as fatal. can we reply with a structured SSE event instructing client to attempt resume? something like: `event: resume-hold\ndata: {"wait_ms":2000}`

elaine: we already have `resume_hint` in protocol but no client consumes it. SDKs need update. still, a conservative server header + short-lived tombstone could prevent dup charge.

sam: also add a console metric: resume_hold_hits and resume_hold_duration so we can measure impact. console-bot: created dashboard tile: Resume hold — count & p50 duration -> https://console/redwood/dashboards/resume-hold

mike: agree on instrumentation. action items: (1) rollback deadtime change to 30s in EU canary now, (2) add resume_hold 3s tombstone + 409 with structured event behind feature flag, (3) SDK follow-up to honor resume_hint (longer path).

elaine: filing ticket now: RDW-PLAT-1129. tagging @sam @mike for review. I'll post a short incident note in #incidents once rollback is scheduled.

sam: quick nudge — let's also add a lint check on config rollouts so deadtime > client_resume by default, otherwise block. caught this once we have SDKs in tree.

mike: ok. thanks team. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy job queued: eu-proxy canary rollback -> 30s (job 53321). logs will show when complete.
